prompts.fixed:
Write one conversation title of at most {max_length} characters, including one relevant emoji. Use this exact layout: EMOJI Topic — action. Keep it near 42 characters by choosing shorter words, never by cutting a word. Rules:
1. Make the requested work clear and faithful. Keep status, uncertainty, negation, and who expressed a view. Investigation is not repair; a proposal is not approval; summarizing customer praise is not praising the subject yourself. Never invent completion.
2. Put the distinguishing topic in the first two meaningful words after the emoji.
3. Use a parallel topic/action structure and stable terms for equivalent requests. Let different topics and genuinely different actions create the differences, not random wording.
4. When relevant, preserve complaint, praise, mixed, or neutral intent.
Use short action labels such as investigate, upgrade/test, explain, summarize feedback, draft proposal, or write note, only when accurate. Return only the title.

USER REQUEST:
{conversation_content}

clarity.instructions: Does this displayed title clearly convey an understandable task or topic? Imperative, noun phrases and topic—action labels are all allowed. Ignore harmless clipping of a modifier when the core task remains clear.

criteria.fail: The core task is unclear or incoherent.
criteria.partial: The core task is partly understandable but its main clause is incomplete or grammatically ambiguous.
criteria.pass: The core task is clear and understandable.

frontload.instructions: Do the first two meaningful lexical words after the emoji identify the distinguishing topic of this request? Ignore punctuation, not ordinary action words; the state includes the exact first two words computed in code.

criteria.fail: The displayed title does not identify a useful distinguishing topic.
criteria.partial: The topic is clear but appears after the first two meaningful words.
criteria.pass: The distinguishing topic appears in the first two meaningful words after the emoji.

fidelity.instructions: Does the title preserve the requested work without an actual wrong action, invented completion/decision, reversed negation, false certainty, or changed attribution? Omission of minor details is allowed. A title naming an inspection or test is compatible with explaining that activity unless it explicitly claims execution or completion. Reporting a completed fix can be factually true but failing to mention writing the requested release note is loss of requested work.

criteria.fail: The title misstates requested work or makes a misleading claim, including praising rather than summarizing customers’ praise.
criteria.pass: The title describes the requested work or a compatible concise topic without a misleading claim.

connotation.instructions: For these customer-feedback or neutral-comparison requests, does the title preserve the input’s sentiment without inventing endorsement or a preference? Explicit mixed feedback counts as both-sided. Generic feedback loses polarity but does not reverse it.

criteria.fail: The title reverses or invents sentiment or preference.
criteria.partial: The title becomes generic/neutral and loses a useful positive, negative or mixed distinction.
criteria.pass: The title preserves the relevant complaint, praise, mixed feedback or neutral comparison intent.

collection.instructions: Judge the sibling titles together. Equivalent requests should use parallel topic/action grammar and stable action terms; meaningful differences in topics or requested actions must remain distinguishable. Ignore emoji, punctuation and compatible abbreviations such as Tests/Regression Tests. A fixed-format label is not required for default titles.

criteria.fail: Equivalent tasks use substantially inconsistent structures, or a meaningful distinction is lost or replaced with invented work.
criteria.partial: Subjects remain distinguishable but there is some arbitrary structural, vocabulary or specificity variation.
criteria.pass: The collection uses parallel structure/stable terms for equivalent tasks and preserves justified topic/action differences.

method: Generate both arms again on all24cases, two repeats, three models; all input/output limits as prior study.
All24requests have been observed in study two; this is a tuned diagnostic set, not held-out validation. Retain original split labels only as historical provenance.
Blind both judges to model/arm labels and each other’s grades. Same questions/criteria and minimal original request/title state for both.
Deduplicate exact request/title outputs once per judge; aggregate occurrences separately. Keep probabilities/confidence from Jev, not proof of truth.
Precompute first two lexical words in code and supply to both judges; compute length/format compliance in code, not by Jev.
Connotation applies only to feedback-family and neutral-compare. Collection rule applies auth/upgrade/feedback/operations separately permodel/arm/repeat.
No adjudication or grade harmonization. Report disagreements and original scores separately. A report review may fix arithmetic or code defects, not rewrite judgments to agreement.
No human gold labels are supplied; judge agreement does not establish accuracy. A small set of prior trouble cases is highlighted rather than presented as ground truth.
limits: Tuned synthetic convenience sample; different generator transports and controls; AI judges may share biases. No human usability study, statistical significance or truth claim.

jev.label_rule: returned choice; preserve probabilities and confidence; do not threshold away disagreements
